mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-25.9 -> -21.6 -> -20.4 -> -17.3), indicating self-reinforcing recovery momentum as consumers resume routine shopping and leisure trips; this momentum should persist and push the 4-week mean higher.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased in each of the last three weekly observations
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the prior 28-day mean despite the three-week rising streak, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained narrowing of the TRANSIT deficit past a -25 threshold signals relaxed travel restrictions or reduced public caution, which mechanically increases access to retail districts and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -25 (less negative than -25) for the current week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -34.3 to -23.7 over four weeks, crossing -25 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -25, the threshold linkage is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects restored commuting patterns that generate combined incidental retail footfall (lunch, errands, after-work shopping), producing a larger RETAIL_REC increase than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -27.3 to -8.6 while TRANSIT rose from -33.1 to -23.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT individually (no synergistic lift), the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A steady decline in RESIDENTIAL time (14.6 -> 10.1 over four weeks) indicates households are spending less time confined at home, a behavioral shift toward outside activity that should translate into increased retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell each week from 14.6 to 10.1
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following two weeks, the behavioral substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high week-to-week volatility (-20.9, -3.6, -11.1, -16.9) consistent with weather-driven outdoor activity swings in May; when PARKS dips sharply it may substitute for indoor retail trips, slightly suppressing RETAIL_REC in the immediate following week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fluctuated between -20.9 and -3.6 over four weeks without a clear trend
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a sharp PARKS decline, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week WORKPLACES jump exceeding 15 points (as seen from -27.3 to -11.6) signals a discrete policy easing event (e.g., office reopening order) that triggers a near-term surge in nearby retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 15.7 points from t-2w (-27.3) to t-1w (-11.6)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week following a WORKPLACES jump exceeding 15 points, the policy-trigger hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near zero (-0.6) after an initial spike, suggesting households have normalized essential shopping and are reallocating spare consumption toward discretionary retail and recreation activities over the coming month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM held near 0 (-0.6 to 0.6) for the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 4 weeks despite stable GROCERY_PHARM readings, the reallocation hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve simultaneously beyond a combined threshold (each improving more than 10 points over two weeks) during a reopening regime, the joint restoration of mobility infrastructure and labor activity produces a disproportionate uplift in RETAIL_REC within two weeks, exceeding what either factor alone would generate.
candidate_trigger: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by more than 10 points over the prior two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.1 to -23.7 and WORKPLACES improved from -27.3 to -8.6 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's rise over the next two weeks is no larger than the sum of effects attributable to TRANSIT and WORKPLACES individually, or if it fails to rise at all, the interaction-regime hypothesis is rejected.
